hashing.source_input_sha256: SHA-256 of the normalized tab-separated prescription extract in the record's evidence.json, UTF-8, LF: it pins the transcription while the publication, the table and the example pin the source. A deferred input has no extract and therefore no hash.
hashing.project_sha256: SHA-256 of the committed project.json file's bytes, UTF-8, LF line endings, one trailing newline
hashing.record_hash: SHA-256 over the record's JSON with record_hash and record_hash_method removed: json.dumps(sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) as UTF-8, no trailing newline

publications.title: Imaging optical system
publications.note: Batch 1 accepted four examples and deferred only Numerical Example 3, as SOURCE_TABLE_INCONSISTENT. That single example is the one input in the whole batch that is a transcription-scale problem rather than a format problem: its [Lens Group Data] prints G1 = 166.46 mm, and the rendered table reproduces that only with surface 9 at -251.1669 mm, while on that reading the system first-order values still come out 529.09 / 34.78 mm against the printed 485.01 / 29.8213 mm. No single or double sign correction reconciles them. A fresh reading of the source, for example the application's own PDF, may settle it. Do not repair it by fitting signs until the numbers close.

opens_questions.question: Does the corpus want zoom prescriptions, and in what form?
opens_questions.detail: A record holds one on-axis configuration (see the configuration_count / configuration_note in any committed record's validation block). A zoom example prints several [Variable Distance Data] columns for the same surface table. Two viable forms exist and need an owner's decision before any of the 46 zoom inputs can be transcribed:
options: One record per zoom position, with the shared prescription repeated and the position named in the record; simple, consistent with the current format, but multiplies the surface tables and risks the records drifting apart.

/workspace/tools/zoom_split.py already does the other form: it splits an imported single-compound Project into per-group components and writes configurations that translate the groups along the axis. That is the native way, and it needs the record format's configuration block, the evidence extract's per-column distances and the batch schema's per-record configuration count to be defined together.
opens_questions.who: A repository maintainer, because it changes the record format, not just a batch.
opens_questions.effect: Until it is answered, batch 2 has nothing to accept. If it is answered, 27 of the 58 inputs become transcribable (13 + 8 + 6, the full-frame zoom publications).

opens_questions.question: Should APS-C and other sub-full-frame publications have their own collection?
opens_questions.detail: US12196935B2 (5 examples) and US20250383527A1 (4 examples) are complete, well-formed tables that batch 1 deferred only because the frame is smaller than full frame. The transcription cost is already paid in the retrieved pages; only the collection boundary blocks them.
opens_questions.effect: Nine inputs, and possibly others in the already-retrieved pages.

opens_questions.detail: One example, one sign ambiguity, and the application's own PDF is image-only so it needs a vision read rather than the HTML table. Low cost, and it would close the only SOURCE_TABLE_INCONSISTENT entry in the batch.

procedure.playbook: /workspace/tools/PLAYBOOK.md — the full pipeline: parse page, draft case, build record, verify, commit.
procedure.verify: Exit code 0 only means the Project imported. Then read record.json -> validation: project_check ACCEPTED, optical_solids VALID, paraxial MATCHED. A DIFFERS paraxial verdict is a defect, never something to explain away.
procedure.deferral: If the source cannot support a faithful transcription, defer with a reason code and do not guess. Batch 1's outcomes list is the precedent for the shape and the wording.
